predictions.prediction_text: The U.S. will impose a 10% supplementary tariff from February 1 on products from several allied European countries, rising to 25% from June 1 unless Greenland is fully sold to the United States.
predictions.condition: agreement on Greenland’s full purchase by the United States
predictions.expected_result: Tariffs remain in place (10% from Feb 1, 25% from Jun 1) until a formal purchase agreement is announced; tariffs are lifted only upon such announcement.

predictions.prediction_text: Europe can sell equities and U.S. Treasuries to exert pressure on Trump ahead of February OpEx if U.S.–EU tensions are not eased.
predictions.condition: U.S.–EU tensions cannot be eased through diplomacy ahead of February options expiration (OpEx)
predictions.expected_result: Net selling pressure from Europe into U.S. equities and Treasury markets increases before February OpEx, leading to downward moves in equities and upward yields (price declines) in Treasuries.

predictions.prediction_text: If the process truly kicks off, we will witness a 20%+ black‑swan event filling the May 9, 2025 gap that is key structural support of the rally.

predictions.prediction_text: Gold is priced higher as markets start to reflect a new regime and elevated long‑term geopolitical risk.

predictions.prediction_text: If inflation returns via tariff pass‑through, wages/energy, or services, the disinflationary boom narrative breaks and bond yields will rise as the bond market demands a higher term premium.

predictions.expected_result: Bond yields increase (term premium and nominal yields rise) significantly relative to prior levels, tightening financial conditions and raising financing costs.

predictions.prediction_text: If banks remain unwilling to lend (NPLs/delinquencies, spread widening, recession fears), the $2.5T of potential additional lending capacity will not be realized.
